# 1 Enoch Chapter 100 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Epistle of Enoch — Woe Oracles (final)

---

**1** In those days, in a single place, fathers will be struck down alongside their sons, and brothers will kill each other, until the rivers are running with blood.

**2** No one will hold back from killing his own sons and grandsons. No sinner will spare even his most honored brother. From morning to evening they will slaughter one another.

**3** Horses will wade through the blood of sinners up to their chests. Chariots will sink in it.

**4** In those days the angels will go down into the hidden places and drag out everyone who helped bring sin into the world. They will gather them all in one place. And the Most High will rise up to execute his great judgment against sinners.

**5** But over every righteous and holy person, God will station guardian angels — holy watchers — to protect them like the apple of his eye, until he has wiped out all wickedness and sin. The righteous may sleep a long sleep, but they have nothing to fear.

**6** Then the people of the earth will see the wise living in safety. They will understand every word in this book. And they will realize that all their wealth could not save them when the day came for their sins to be overthrown.

**7** Woe to you, sinners, on the day of crushing anguish — you who torment the righteous and burn them alive — you will receive exactly what you gave.

**8** Woe to you, hardhearted ones, who lie awake scheming evil — terror will seize you and there will be no one to help.

**9** Woe to you, sinners — for what you have said and what you have done in your godlessness. You will burn in blazing fires, hotter than anything you have ever known.

**10** And hear this: from the angels, God will gather testimony about your deeds. From the sun and moon and stars he will gather evidence — because of how you oppressed the righteous while you ruled the earth.

**11** Every cloud, every mist, every drop of dew, every raindrop will be summoned to testify against you. They will all be withheld from you because of your sins. No dew. No rain.

**12** So go ahead — bribe the rain. Offer it your gold and silver. See if it will take the payment and fall anyway.

**13** And when the frost comes, and the snow, and the bitter cold, and all the storms pour down on you — in that day, you will not be able to stand.

---

*PNEUMA notes: V. 12 is sarcastically devastating — the Epistle invites sinners to try bribing the rain with the same gold they used to bribe judges. Nature cannot be corrupted. Vv. 1–3's image of blood flooding streams and horses wading in gore is among the most extreme apocalyptic violence imagery in Second Temple literature. V. 5's angelic protection of the righteous — "apple of an eye" — is the tender center of this blood-soaked chapter.*
